completed_work: Source-first connected draft of seven complete chapters: 216 verses, each with before/after wording, TSW comparator, exact original Hebrew record hash and individual rationale.
Selective Notes and Vocabulary support recognizable terms, source imagery, speakers and consequential ambiguity.
All 48 cumulative source-binding ledger audits passed, totaling 6,618 verses across 216 chapters. Structure, translation-family, focused assertions and diff checks passed.
All 658 verses of Joshua now have a revised draft; whole-book authoring consistency review remains next.
key_decisions: 18 retains seven divisions, three male surveyors per tribe, priestly service as Levi’s inheritance, and the distinction between allotted land and possession.

18:15 keeps the difficult westward direction; 18:18 keeps Arabah without supplying Beth-arabah. 18:24 follows reading-tradition Chephar-ammonah; 18:28 separates Gibeath and Kiriath with an alternative noted.

19 retains Beer-sheba and Sheba beside the stated thirteen towns, five closing Zebulun names beside twelve, and sixteen Naphtali names beside nineteen. It neither drops names nor invents missing entries.

19:22 uses reading-tradition Shahazimah rather than written-form Shahazumah. 19:34 preserves Judah at the Jordan. 19:47 interprets loss of territory, notes an alternative, and preserves the conquest and killing at Leshem.
20 distinguishes accidental killing from prior hatred, protects resident foreigners as well as Israelites, and keeps both until-judgment and until-high-priest-death conditions.

21 preserves all forty-eight town-and-pasture grants, including 36–37 present in the pinned source, the repeated Gath-rimmon, and the distinction between Caleb’s fields/villages and Levitical pasturelands.
21:43–45 retains all-land, rest and total-fulfillment claims beside chapter 23’s remaining nations and future expulsion.
22 preserves the altar dispute’s reported geography, threatened war, offer to share western land, accusations and conditional denials, and repeated concern about children losing a share in the LORD.

22:20 keeps Achan son of Zerah and that he did not die alone. 22:22 repeats three divine names twice and leaves the singular appeal’s addressee open. 22:31 keeps rescue from the LORD’s hand; 22:34 identifies Witness as a supplied name.
23 preserves the causative oath expression, one-to-thousand image, intermarriage, traps/whips/thorns and repeated not-one-word-failed formula, with divine harm and threatened loss explicit.
24 preserves the shifts between ancestors/you and LORD/he/I, Balak’s fighting, all seven peoples, the hornet and two kings, and the household pledge without harmonizing the retelling.
24:19–23 retains cannot serve, will not forgive and foreign gods among the present people. 24:26–27 keeps the sanctuary setting and the stone that hears, including the us-to-you witness shift.
24 retains Joshua’s age of 110, all three burial notices, Joseph’s bones, one hundred qesitahs consistent with Genesis 33:19, and the hill given to Eleazar’s son.
remaining_review_questions: Independent Hebrew review remains required, especially the boundary syntax and naming at 18:15,18,28; 19:2,8,13,15,27,29,33–34,38,47.
The two temporal conditions in 20:6, textual history of 21:36–37, geographic report in 22:10–11, singular appeal in 22:22 and implied altar name at 22:34 need independent review.
Whole-book Joshua consistency review must address inheritance/share, serve, cling, witness, instruction, divine war/fulfillment and remaining peoples without harmonizing distinct statements.
Reader comprehension and sustained listening have not been tested. Overlap metrics cannot certify independent authorship, fidelity or biblical fluency.
overlap_qualification: Normalized whole-verse overlap is triage only, not fidelity, originality, comprehension or independent approval.
